Subject: ACME POC - proposed scope & next steps

Hi Jordan / Emily —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps for the 4-week POC we discussed.

High-level POC goal:
- Validate Redwood inference for ACME’s customer-support summarization pipeline at target latency (~150ms per request) and accuracy (>= 92% QA score vs. your rubric).

Success criteria (proposal):
- Latency: median end-to-end < 200ms for 95th percentile interactive queries in your sandbox.
- Quality: >= 92% agreement with ACME QA rubric on a 100-sample test set.
- Cost: baseline unit cost estimate and one optimization pass using batching + quantization.
- Integrations: end-to-end demo using your staging data, streaming responses, and one example of tool calling for knowledge-base lookup.

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): scope confirmation, NDA/procurement, sandbox credentials, and kickoff (target 2026-12-02).
- Week 1: SDK integration + sample payloads; smoke tests.
- Week 2: quality eval & tuning; implement streaming & tool-calling flow.
- Week 3: performance tuning (batching/kvs), cost projection.
- Week 4: joint demo, success criteria check, next-phase recommendation.

Ownership (Redwood / ACME):
- Redwood: Vivek (SE) — technical integration & runbook; Rishi (CS) — trial health & metrics; Marissa — program lead / escalation.
- ACME: Jordan — engineering lead; Emily — product / evaluation lead.

Immediate asks:
1) Please confirm the success criteria above or propose edits.
2) Sandbox credentials & a list of ~10 sample queries and the QA rubric by EOD Monday (2026-11-30).
3) Any procurement or legal blockers we should track now (NDA, SOW, etc).

Attaching: POC-scope.xlsx and our Redwood integration playbook (PDF). I’ll follow up with Vivek’s integration notes.

Thanks — Marissa

Jordan — quick technical notes to help your staging team align. Summary first, then specifics.

Summary:
- Auth: Redwood supports API key auth for POCs (sent via Authorization: Bearer <key>) and OAuth for longer-term integrations. For now, we’ll provide a sandbox API key (redacted) and scoped short-lived keys for your engineers.
- SDKs: Official SDKs in Python, Node, and Go. We recommend starting with the Python SDK for quick testing.
- Endpoints: Text generation endpoint is POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (streaming enabled with ?stream=true or via SDK stream() API).
- Tool calling: Yes — structured tool calls supported. You can register a tool that accepts a JSON schema; Redwood will send the structured args in the call payload. We also surface tool invocation events in the response stream so clients can react in real time.

Technical details / snippets:
- cURL (streaming):
  curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <SANDBOX_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","prompt":"Summarize support thread:","stream":true}' \
    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"

- Python SDK (stream example):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<SANDBOX_KEY>")
  for chunk in client.generate_stream(model='gpt-redwood-1', prompt='Summarize...'):
      print(chunk.text)

- Tool calling example (tool registered server-side):
  request -> Redwood inference -> tool_invocation event in stream -> your service gets POST /tool-hook with args JSON -> your service replies -> Redwood continues generation with tool result.

Integration checklist (for Week 1):
- Provide sandbox API key + IP allowlist (if you use one) — Redwood will supply.
- Confirm sample payloads and expected fields (we’ll map your request/response schema).
- Run smoke test: >100 sample requests for latency baseline.
- Verify streaming client receives tool_invocation events and can POST back to our callback URL (we’ll provide a test stub).

Potential blockers: If you enforce mTLS or have a strict proxy policy, send network requirements and we’ll coordinate.

Happy to jump on a brief tech call. Proposed slot: Tue 2026-12-01 10:00 PT — does that work?

— Vivek
